system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel – Buyer-side review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**To:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Status:** Privileged / buyer internal

## 1. Threshold point: the "pre-categorisation" and "FINAL" labels

Before the substance: the Seller's package asks us to treat everything marked [STANDARD] as "reviewed and cleared by both sides" and to review only [OPEN] items (of which there are none). We should not accept that framing.

- Nothing in our instructions records a principal-level agreement to these positions. If the deal team has in fact agreed any of them, tell me and I will reflect it, but a counterparty's draft asserting that the other side has already agreed is not evidence of agreement.
- The "market context" paragraph is advocacy. Some of those ranges are seen in the market, but they are usually seen together with W&I insurance, a clean disclosure process and no live issues. This deal has at least five live, quantifiable issues (below), which is exactly when buyers move off "market" packages.
- Recommended response: reply that the Buyer does not accept any clause as cleared, that all clauses remain open, and that the review and mark-up proceed on that basis.

I have reviewed every clause regardless of label.

## 2. Material issues and reasoning

### 2.1 Riverlark facility (cl 2/7) – deal-structural, must be fixed

The deal is debt-free/cash-free, yet AUD 3.2m is outstanding, the facility has a change-of-control trigger (8.1) and the Seller proposes a release "following Completion". That is inconsistent with the headline price mechanics:

- If the debt is still in the Company at Completion, Wattlebridge is effectively paying AUD 24m plus assuming AUD 3.2m – a ~13% price increase.
- Completing while 8.1 is unsatisfied likely puts the Company in default on day one, with security still registered (and, probably, security over the shares themselves – see 2.11).

**Push back:** Repayment at Completion out of the Seller's proceeds via the funds flow; payout letter, deed of release and PPSR discharge (or irrevocable undertaking to discharge) delivered as Completion deliverables; alternatively, treat the outstanding amount as Debt deducted from the price. No post-Completion release.

### 2.2 Bluefen consent (cl 3/6.3) – ~30% of revenue, condition is drafted around

Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue. DD-002 cl 11.2 requires consent on change of control and cl 11.3 attaches conditions. The Seller's draft (a) only commits to "reasonable endeavours" and (b) deems the condition satisfied on delivery of "written consent" – which sidesteps the 11.3 conditions entirely. The Disclosure Letter confirms no consent and no evidence the conditions are satisfied.

**Push back:** Unconditional written consent (or conditions satisfied, in a form reasonably satisfactory to the Buyer) as a condition precedent waivable only by the Buyer; "all reasonable endeavours" plus a positive obligation not to agree to variations of the Bluefen terms without Buyer consent; long-stop date; and a price adjustment / escrow fallback if the Buyer elects to complete without consent. Add a warranty that no notice of termination or non-renewal has been received from Bluefen.

### 2.3 Closing bonuses (DD-005) – AUD 420k leakage plus on-costs

The Seller says the bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" but the Company is the employer and will pay them. If they are not in the funds flow, Wattlebridge funds them after Completion. Add superannuation (~12%) and NSW payroll tax (~5.45%) and the true cost is nearer AUD 490k.

**Push back:** Either (i) Seller pays the bonuses (grossed up for super, payroll tax and on-costs) through the funds flow at Completion, or (ii) the grossed-up amount is treated as Debt/Transaction Expenses and deducted from the price. Also confirm who bears any bonuses that vest after Completion on "continued employment" – these should still be Seller cost since they are triggered by the Seller's sale.

### 2.4 Ironquay IP (cl 11.1) – ownership of platform IP

DD-004 cl 7.3 says SOW3 Project Materials transfer only on payment of every SOW3 fee; AUD 180k is open and there is no receipt or confirmatory assignment. For a SaaS target, developed code that may still be owned by a contractor is a core-asset risk, not an administrative one. The Seller's indemnity capped at the SOW3 payment covers the wrong thing – the exposure is not the 180k but loss of (or a licence dispute over) the IP.

**Push back:** Pre-Completion covenant / Completion deliverable: pay SOW3 fees, obtain written receipt and a confirmatory deed of assignment (with moral rights consents) from Ironquay. Specific indemnity for all loss arising from any IP in the platform not vesting in the Company (including replacement/re-development cost and third-party claims), not limited to the SOW3 fee, outside the basket, cap at purchase price, and a longer time limit. Unqualified IP ownership warranty.

### 2.5 Data export incident (cl 4.6 / Sch 6, DD-006) – not "preliminary" from our side

~1,240 records sent to an unintended external address. The data is business-contact rather than sensitive, which may help on the "likely to result in serious harm" test, but the Seller's own disclosure says they do not know whether the file was accessed, the scope, or whether notification is required. Under the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme the Company has 30 days to complete its assessment; the incident predates 22 September, so that window is either closed or closing. Characterising it as "not expected to be material" is a Seller assertion, not a fact; and the general disclosure is designed to make the privacy warranties worthless on this point.

**Push back:** Covenant to complete the assessment (and notify OAIC/individuals if required) before Completion, with Buyer visibility; specific indemnity for all costs, penalties, notification, remediation and third-party claims arising from the incident, outside basket/cap-on-general-warranties; express statement that DD-006 does not qualify the privacy/data warranties. If the Seller insists the matter is immaterial, it should cost them nothing to indemnify.

### 2.6 General cap (cl 12.1) – 20% is too low for this risk profile

AUD 4.8m sounds like a meaningful number until you note that the identified issues alone (Riverlark 3.2m, Bluefen 3.6m revenue, bonuses ~0.49m, Sandbar 0.33m, Ironquay, data incident) exceed it. A 20% cap is defensible where W&I insurance sits above it; here there is none.

**Push back:** General warranty cap of 50% (open to 100%) without W&I; or 20% cap with Seller-funded W&I policy and a nil/low seller retention; fundamental, title and tax warranties and all specific indemnities capped at 100% of price. Given the Seller is a venture vehicle that may distribute proceeds, add a retention/escrow (10–15% for 18–24 months) or parent/fund guarantee.

### 2.7 Thresholds (cl 12.2)

De minimis of 25k plus a 250k deductible basket (excess only) is Seller-favourable on both limbs.

**Push back:** De minimis 10–15k; basket at ~0.5–1% but tipping (first-dollar recovery once exceeded); related claims aggregated; fundamental/title/tax warranties and specific indemnities excluded from both thresholds. Note the Sandbar structure (three × 110k) shows the Seller is comfortable splitting items – aggregation language matters.

### 2.8 Time limits (cl 12.3/13) and the "applies to all Claims" sweep

18 months general is tolerable (24 months preferred, to cover a full audit cycle). The real problem is the proposal that any limitation applies to "all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" – that catches tax, title, indemnities and covenants by default.

**Push back:** Tax warranties/indemnity: 7 years (or statutory period for amendment + 6 months). Title/capacity: no limit, or 6 years minimum. Specific indemnities: 6 years. Completion obligations, restrictive covenants and leakage: ordinary limitation. Reverse the default: limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims unless expressly extended.

### 2.9 Fundamental/title warranties under general regime – reject outright

"Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to cap title. If the Seller cannot deliver title to 100% of the shares, the Buyer's loss is the full price. Title and capacity warranties must be uncapped (or capped at price), unlimited in time, outside thresholds and not qualified by disclosure.

### 2.10 Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance applying to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5)

**Push back:** Carve out fraud, wilful concealment and wilful misconduct; specific indemnities; tax indemnity; breach of pre-Completion and Completion covenants; leakage; restrictive covenants. Non-reliance should be confined to statements outside the SPA, disclosure letter and documents expressly listed; it must not attempt to exclude liability for misleading or deceptive conduct under the Australian Consumer Law (which cannot be contracted out of in any case). Equitable remedies (injunction/specific performance) for covenants must survive.

### 2.11 Disclosure standard (Sch 7, Disclosure Letter 1.1/1.2) and buyer knowledge (cl 8.3)

These two clauses together effectively neutralise the warranty package:

- General disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012) and all "publicly searchable corporate records" means any matter buried in any document, or in any register anywhere, qualifies every warranty.
- Cl 8.3 then removes claims for anything the Buyer "or its advisers" knew or that was "discoverable" from the data room or public records – constructive knowledge, extended to advisers.
- The Disclosure Letter's cut-off is 5pm 22 September 2026; we are now in November, so it is already stale.

**Push back:** Fair-disclosure standard ("disclosed with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter and its likely impact"); disclosure of the data room limited to specific documents by index number, and of public records limited to listed ASIC, PPSR and IP Australia searches on a stated date. Delete cl 8.3, or at most limit to actual knowledge of two or three named Wattlebridge individuals, excluding advisers, excluding "discoverable", and not applying to specific indemnities or fundamental warranties. Require a bring-down of warranties at Completion; any new disclosure between signing and Completion goes to the Buyer's termination/price-adjustment rights only and does not qualify warranties for claims. Paragraph 1.4 (non-admission) is acceptable only if it does not limit what is "fairly disclosed".

### 2.12 Title verification (DD-012)

The Disclosure Letter is carefully worded: it identifies the share register as "the source relied on" and notes the Buyer has not done its own verification – an attempt to shift title risk onto buyer knowledge. A share register is only prima facie evidence (Corporations Act s 176).

**Action:** Run current ASIC company and PPSR searches (expect Riverlark security over shares and assets), obtain share certificates, confirm no options, convertibles, shareholder agreements or pre-emption rights, and obtain Riverlark's release over the shares at Completion. Title warranty to be absolute and not qualified by DD-012.

### 2.13 Sandbar renewals (DD-008/DD-011) – AUD 330k

Three identical AUD 110k renewals, disclosed across two documents to be "read together" – the splitting warrants scrutiny (contract-materiality thresholds, approval limits). The Seller does not say whether they are committed, accrued or terminable.

**Push back:** Obtain the agreements; if committed pre-Completion and relating to the pre-Completion period, treat as Debt/working-capital adjustment; if genuinely ordinary course and forward-looking, confirm in the warranty schedule and ensure they are reflected in the normalised working capital target.

### 2.14 Tax and IP warranties "settled under the general regime"

Reject for both. Tax: full tax warranty suite plus a pre-Completion tax indemnity, 7-year period, cap at price. IP: for a SaaS target, IP ownership/non-infringement/open-source warranties should sit in the higher-cap tier (at least 50%, preferably 100%) with a longer period.

### 2.15 Lower-priority items

- **Office lease (DD-007):** notification obligation only. Make the notification a Completion deliverable and obtain a copy of the lease to confirm there is no change-of-control or landlord-consent provision hidden elsewhere.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** anti-assignment is not triggered by a share sale on its face; confirm the clause has no change-of-control limb and add it to the material-contracts warranty.

## 3. Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Position to take |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | "Pre-cleared / FINAL" framing | Reject; all clauses open |
| 2 | Riverlark AUD 3.2m | Repay at Completion from Seller proceeds; release/discharge as Completion deliverable; else deduct as Debt |
| 3 | Bluefen consent | Unconditional consent (11.3 satisfied) as Buyer-waivable CP; all-reasonable-endeavours; price adjustment/escrow fallback |
| 4 | Closing bonuses | Seller funds AUD 420k grossed up for super/payroll tax/on-costs via funds flow, or deduct as Debt |
| 5 | Ironquay IP | Pay SOW3, confirmatory assignment pre-Completion; indemnity for all IP-vesting loss, capped at price, outside basket |
| 6 | Data incident | Complete NDB assessment pre-Completion; specific indemnity; DD-006 not to qualify privacy warranties |
| 7 | General cap | 50–100% without W&I, or 20% with Seller-funded W&I; retention/escrow 10–15% |
| 8 | Thresholds | De minimis 10–15k; tipping basket 0.5–1%; aggregation; indemnities/fundamentals excluded |
| 9 | Time limits | General 24m; tax 7y; title unlimited; indemnities 6y; reverse the "applies to all Claims" default |
| 10 | Fundamental/title | Uncapped (or price), unlimited, not subject to disclosure or thresholds |
| 11 | Exclusive remedy / non-reliance | Carve out fraud, indemnities, covenants, leakage, ACL |
| 12 | Disclosure standard | Fair-disclosure test; specific documents only; no blanket public-record disclosure; refresh and bring-down |
| 13 | Buyer knowledge cl 8.3 | Delete, or actual knowledge of named individuals only |
| 14 | Title verification | Buyer to run ASIC/PPSR; absolute title warranty; share security released at Completion |
| 15 | Sandbar AUD 330k | Obtain contracts; classify as Debt/working capital or confirm ordinary course |
| 16 | Tax / IP warranties | Separate tiers: tax indemnity 7y; IP at higher cap |
| 17 | Lease / Mossvale | Completion deliverables and warranty coverage; verify underlying clauses |

**Suggested sequencing for the response letter:** lead with items 2–6 (structural and quantified – these are the ones with the clearest money attached and the least room for a "market" argument), then the limitation package (7–13) as a connected whole, since the Seller's disclosure and knowledge clauses are what make the cap and thresholds dangerous rather than merely tight.

Let me know if any of these positions were in fact agreed at principal level and I will revise the mark-up priorities accordingly.
=== END ADVICE ===
